Reference: Albouy, B. (2026). Homeostatic Economics — A methodological and conceptual reference framework for macroeconomic viability in a biophysically finite world. Working paper, version 1.0.
English translation produced with AI from the French original, “Calibration empirique de l'Économie Homéostatique — rapport d'étape v1.6”, which is the authoritative version.
<b>En bref.</b> Ce rapport rend compte d: In brief. This report gives an account of a first stage of empirical calibration of HE’s formal framework. It consisted in linking the objects of the V1.0 formalization (§5.5 of the WP) to traceable public data, recomputing the parameter βpub of note 47, gathering the candidate series for the three components of the biophysical state S = (BDI, EFI, NRRI), then measuring the sensitivity of the DEI to the construction choices that the WP leaves open, with published normative benchmarks for the value 1. These results are shown on a public map, with cross-border divisions on which to reason when defining buffer zones. The WP’s ecodotation formulas are applied there to public data, to give their calibration a first order of magnitude. No value produced is a measurement of the DEI: all depend on explicit choices, documented with them.
Le WP V1.0 formalise l'EH comme un systè: The WP V1.0 formalizes HE as a controlled dynamical system: a state x = (S, M), where S = (BDI, EFI, NRRI) groups three exo-economic indicators normalized on [0, 2] and M the money stock; a prescribed feedback u = Φ(DEI(S)), where the DEI is the geometric mean of the three components of S; a viability corridor K = KS × KM. The framework poses viability as the primary question and refers to a research programme the characterization of the classes of models and rules compatible with a non-empty viability kernel (FP1).
Ce formalisme ne prend appui sur la réal: This formalism rests on biophysical and economic reality only through measurable quantities: the sub-indicators of S, the thresholds that delimit K, the institutional parameters of the ecodotations. The aim of the stage described here is to build this link reproducibly:
rattacher chaque objet de la formalisati: link each object of the formalization to the public data that can feed it, or establish that none exists;
recalculer les paramètres déjà calibrés: recompute the parameters already calibrated in the WP, to make them verifiable by a reader;
rendre visibles et chiffrables les choix: make visible and quantifiable the construction choices that the WP leaves open (normalization, aggregation, weightings), in connection with problems T3, E4 and I5;
le faire dans une infrastructure où chaq: do so within an infrastructure in which every figure can be traced back to the downloaded file, archived, and recomputed automatically when the sources are updated.
L'enjeu de recherche qui oriente l'ensem: The research issue guiding the whole is how accurately the indicators represent biophysical reality: the performativity of the system depends on it (axiom A4). This criterion guided the choices described below, in particular the use of absolute benchmarks expressed as physical quantities per inhabitant and the attention paid to the geographical scale of the indicators.
2. Point de départ et choix de l'infrast: 2. Starting point and choice of infrastructure
Le point de départ est une série de proj: The starting point is a series of projects published in November 2026. Andrej Karpathy presented usaciv, a map of the United States in the style of a strategy game, built from 31 public sources merged on a hexagonal grid. The project was adapted to France (franceciv), then to Europe (europeciv, repository lmveprog/Europe-Civilization). These projects pursue no analytical aim; their interest for HE lies in their method: a pipeline that downloads public sources, formats them and brings them onto a common grid, with the provenance of each file.

<b>Licence.</b> Le code est sous licence: Licence. The code is under the MIT licence: it can be reused, modified and published provided the licence notice is kept. The data keep their own licences, almost all open (CC BY 4.0, Licence Ouverte, public domain).
<b>Traçabilité.</b> La chaîne suit toujo: Traceability. The pipeline always follows the same path (source, intermediate data, build) and records, for each download, its address, date and SHA-256 fingerprint.
<b>Sobriété technique.</b> La chaîne n'u: Technical sobriety. The pipeline uses only the Python standard library, which makes it easy to read and run.
<b>Échelle géographique.</b> La grille h: Geographical scale. The hexagonal grid, covering land and sea, will be able to accommodate sub-national and cross-border data once integrated (section 7).

The computations are run there by GitHub Actions, which downloads the data directly from Eurostat. Each run constitutes a batch: raw responses, manifests and execution environment are archived and published under the batch name, and the batch is recorded only if its offline replay yields the same series (section 10).

Ce constat a fixé l'ordre du travail : c: This finding set the order of work: start with the only parameter already defined and verifiable end to end (β<sub>pub</sub>), then gather the candidate series for the three components of S, without computing the indicators themselves as long as their references and normalization are not specified.
La note 47 du WP calibre β<sub>pub</sub>: Note 47 of the WP calibrates β<sub>pub</sub> at €22,000 (rounded value, constant 2017 euros): the average public expenditure per inhabitant of the ten EU-27 Member States where it is highest, computed on 2017 data published in 2019 (€22,310). The eh_beta_pub module reproduces this calculation: total general government expenditure (gov_10a_main, sector S13, item TE, millions of euros) and average annual population from the national accounts (nama_10_pe). For other years, conversion to constant 2017 euros using the EU-27 implicit GDP deflator (nama_10_gdp) is an extension of the fork: the WP sets the 2017 benchmark without prescribing a deflator.
Le recalcul sur les données actuelles re: The recomputation on current data finds the same ten countries, in the same order (Luxembourg, Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Austria, Belgium, France, Netherlands, Germany, Ireland), and gives €22,589 per inhabitant, i.e. 1.25% more than the unrounded value of note 47. This gap is consistent with revisions to the series since 2019; its exact origin would require the data released in 2019. The rounded value of €22,000 remains defensible as an exploratory institutional parameter; a reproducible figure requires stating the extraction batch.
Source : lot calibration-eh-20261128T071: Source: batch calibration-eh-20261128T0719Z, direct Eurostat extraction. Flags: values marked provisional, estimated, break in series or different definition. Margin: gap between the 10th and 11th country (Italy every year), relative to the 10th.
Le choix du groupe et de la pondération: The choice of group and weighting weighs more than the revision gap. On the same 2017 data: average of the ten countries weighted by population, €19,493; average of the 27 countries, €12,867; total expenditure of the 27 countries relative to their population, €13,933; median country, €8,948. The convention of note 47 is one convention among others: historical public expenditure includes transfers and institutional structures specific to each country, and does not directly measure a need for primary money creation. β<sub>pub</sub> is a harmonization parameter to be calibrated.
<b>Variante en standards de pouvoir d'ac: Purchasing power standards (PPS) variant. The same convention, applied to expenditure per inhabitant divided by each country’s GDP price level index (prc_ppp_ind, EU-27 = 100), gives PPS 18,855 in 2017, the ten countries retained being LU, DK, AT, BE, SE, FR, FI, DE, NL, IT. An amount in PPS represents the same purchasing power in each country; it is converted back into euros using the country’s price level index (section 9.3). The price level retained is that of GDP, which covers all production.
<b>2017 comme millésime de référence.</b: 2017 as reference year. No value for the 27 countries or the deflator carries a Eurostat flag, the selection margin is 12.2%, and it is the WP’s reference year. The 2016–2019 series is stable (€22,500 to €23,000 constant). Amounts rise from €22,969 in 2019 to €24,703 in 2020 and remain at that level: an automatically recalibrated parameter would also transmit crisis policies, and a freezing or smoothing rule is a separate choice, to be justified.
<b>Données 2025 conservées, non utilisée: 2025 data kept, not used. Fourteen values carry a provisional flag. The monthly computation indicates when a year no longer carries any; stability is then observed from one batch to the next.
<b>Déflateur du PIB plutôt que l'indice: GDP deflator rather than the consumer price index, because it covers all production. It corrects neither national price levels nor the composition of expenditure; a purchasing power parity variant is to be compared.
<b>Vérification par extraction directe.<: Verification by direct extraction. The first values had been read indirectly from Eurostat pages; execution on GitHub Actions, which downloads the files themselves, confirmed the 2017 and 2025 amounts to the euro, and the ASTRA-EC intermediate review recomputed them with a separate program for all eleven years.
5. Séries candidates des composantes de: 5. Candidate series for the components of S
Le WP présente chacun des trois indicate: The WP presents each of the three indicators as the result of a construction chain: data, sub-indicators, protocols, normalization (§6.2). Three modules gather the public series available at Member State level, without computing the indicators. The table codes were established by consulting the full Eurostat catalogue; reading requires the expected codes and stops with an error if a table’s schema changes.
Séries : consommation intérieure de mati: Series: domestic material consumption (DMC, env_ac_mfa) and material footprint (RMC, env_ac_rme), per inhabitant, for metal ores (MF2), non-metallic minerals (MF3) and fossil energy materials (MF4). DMC covers the 27 countries from 2010 to 2025. Total RMC is published for the 27 countries; its breakdown by material category is published for 15, usually up to 2023. The sensitivity analysis uses total RMC (section 6.1).
La DMC additionne l'extraction intérieur: DMC adds domestic extraction and imports, minus exports, in direct weight; RMC attributes to final demand the extraction mobilized in global production chains. For metals, French RMC is five times DMC: the choice between the two measures is decisive, and the data here quantify the point of vigilance in §6.2 on international trade. These are flows: they inform about pressure; the availability horizon of a resource, its criticality or its recyclability belong to stocks and to other data.
5.2 IEE — pressions sur les écosystèmes: 5.2 EFI — pressures on ecosystems and renewable resources
Indice d'exploitation de l'eau (WEI+) :: Water exploitation index (WEI+): net consumption relative to renewable resources
Trois enseignements pour la spécificatio: Three lessons for the specification. Publication rhythms are heterogeneous (annual for emissions, every three years for land take), which introduces a delay in the signal. The national average erases local tensions: water exploitation is 3.2% for France as a whole, whereas tensions are seasonal and specific to certain basins, a concrete case of problem M4. Finally, France’s consumption footprint (8.1 t CO<sub>2</sub> eq./inh, 2024) exceeds the emissions of its resident units (5.9 t) by about 40%; among the pressures retained for the EFI, only climate is published on the consumption side. The Eurostat tables consulted contain no national series on habitat fragmentation.
Oiseaux communs, toutes espèces et forêt: Common birds, all species and forests
Une seule série mesure l'état du vivant: Only one series measures the state of living systems by country, and partially: the common farmland bird index, relative to a base year specific to each country (2000 for most; 1998 for Austria, 2004 for Portugal, 2005 for Slovakia, 2006 for Cyprus, 2007 for Greece, 2008 for Slovenia, 2010 for Luxembourg). It describes national trends; its levels are not comparable from one country to another. Protected areas measure an effort, drought a disturbance; genetic diversity and ecosystem diversity have no national series at Eurostat. A broader source on state lies outside Eurostat: the conservation status of habitats and species reported under Article 17 of the Habitats Directive, by biogeographical region and by country (European Environment Agency, every six years).
Production ou consommation ; flux ou sto: Production or consumption; flows or stocks; sustainable reference per inhabitant
Séries non annuelles ; échelle spatiale: Non-annual series; spatial scale; attribution principle; internal aggregation
Sources hors Eurostat ; distinguer état: Sources outside Eurostat; distinguish state and protection effort
Les trois composantes n'ont pas la même: The three components do not have the same data quality. With a geometric mean with equal exponents, each component has the same weight in the DEI, whatever the quality of its measurement; the uncertainty of the DEI then depends on the errors of each component, their variances and their covariances (T3). Data quality, a criterion cited by E4 for the weightings, differs markedly from one component to another. The detailed summary note is in calibration/NOTE_SYNTHESE.md.
La normalisation sur [0, 2] demande une: Normalization on [0, 2] requires a reference value (the value 1) for each sub-indicator. Two options were considered: relative benchmarks, such as the EU average at a given date, or absolute benchmarks expressed as physical quantities per inhabitant. The second was retained: an average enshrines current consumption habits, which the literature places beyond sustainability benchmarks, and says nothing about the biophysical state. The benchmarks retained are published normative benchmarks — targets, budgets or global limits — allocated in equal shares per inhabitant; each is used as a reference scenario, with its nature and scope. Where no benchmark is retained, the unknown is declared rather than filled in.
Budget 2011–2100 (1 000 Gt, 2 °C) répart: 2011–2100 budget (1,000 Gt, 2 °C) allocated per inhabitant per year
Azote fixé, engrais minéraux et fixation: Fixed nitrogen, mineral fertilizers and biological fixation (kg/inh)
Limite planétaire globale répartie par h: Global planetary boundary allocated per inhabitant
Limite définie à l'échelle régionale, ré: Boundary defined at regional scale, allocated per inhabitant
Les valeurs d'O'Neill répartissent des g: O'Neill’s values allocate global quantities for about 7 billion inhabitants; for a fixed global quantity, 8 billion reduce the per-inhabitant share by 12.5%. Equality per inhabitant is a distributive rule; historical responsibilities and differentiated needs call for other rules, to be compared.
<b>Mesure de l'IRNR.</b> L'IRNR est calc: Measurement of the NRRI. The NRRI is computed on the total material footprint (RMC), biomass included: this is the scope of the two published benchmarks, and the series covers the 27 Member States. This choice has a counterpart: the component no longer measures the WP’s NRRI object, the consumption of non-renewable resources, but total material pressure; biomass, which is renewable, overlaps the scope of the EFI. No published benchmark covers the non-renewable share alone, and the breakdown of RMC by material category is published for only some countries. The gap between the object defined by the framework and what the available data and benchmarks make it possible to measure shows the difficulty of producing and using indicators for a theoretical object. The non-renewable share (MF2–MF4) is computed as a variant (section 6.3).
<b>Inconnues déclarées.</b> Eau douce :: Declared unknowns. Fresh water: O'Neill’s benchmark (574 m³/inh/yr of blue water) applies to a consumption footprint, with no homogeneous national series; WEI+ measures net consumption relative to the territory’s renewable resources, also published by basin and by season, with a conventional stress threshold (20%). Water is kept out of the DEI by construction choice, so as not to aggregate a territorial tension with global per-inhabitant benchmarks; its integration by basin is an open avenue. Land take: no per-inhabitant benchmark retained. Gases other than CO2: specific benchmark to be established. Non-renewable resources alone: specific benchmark to be established, on a stock logic. BDI: treated as an unknown, explored through scenarios (section 6.2).
Le WP fixe l'échelle, la valeur 1 et le: The WP fixes the scale, the value 1 and the direction of the transformation, but not the form of the normalization function nor the position of benchmarks 0 and 2. Three candidate forms, built for the analysis, are tested: linear (2 − x/T, zero at twice the benchmark), ratio (T/x, capped at 2) and hyperbolic (2/(1 + x/T), never zero); the placement of the values 0 and 2 imposed by each form is a numerical choice. They are crossed with four aggregation functions (geometric mean of V1.0, power means ρ = −1 and ρ = −5, minimum), applied both between the sub-indicators of the EFI and between the components of the DEI, four sets of weightings, the two NRRI benchmarks and five BDI values common to all countries (0; 0.5; 1; 1.5; 2), i.e. 480 configurations, which give 198 distinct score vectors to nine decimal places. Three experiments complete the grid: modified aggregation at a single stage; a country-specific BDI (0.5 for that country, 1 for the others); the NRRI computed on the non-renewable share alone (MF2–MF4). The hyperbolic form serves as the reference configuration for presentation, because it is defined without truncation over the whole domain.
Règles de mesure : une série absente pou: Measurement rules: a series missing for 2023 is replaced by the most recent of the three preceding years; a sum and a ratio are formed from terms of the same year, population included; values carrying a Eurostat flag are retained and flagged. Rank correlations are computed on unrounded scores, with average ranks in case of ties, and are not applicable when the DEI is identical for all countries. The envelopes are sets of scenarios, without probability.
Année 2023. Référence : normalisation hy: Year 2023. Reference: hyperbolic normalization, geometric mean at both stages, equal weights, NRRI benchmark of 7.2 t, BDI assumed equal to 1. The envelope covers the whole grid, BDI from 0 to 2 included. Twenty countries have all the series: this is an availability subset, whose averages and ranks describe these countries only.
Chaque ligne fait varier un seul choix à: Each row varies a single choice from the reference. Beyond six inverted pairs, their number is given; the list is in calibration/SENSIBILITE_IED.md. With the geometric mean, a common BDI multiplies all scores by the same factor: the ranking is invariant by construction.
IBD propre à un pays : 0,5 pour ce pays,: Country-specific BDI: 0.5 for that country, 1 for the others. Hypothetical scenario; none of these values is an observation.
<b>Variante de périmètre.</b> Rapportée: Scope variant. Relative to the same benchmarks, the non-renewable share of the footprint alone (MF2–MF4) makes it possible to compute the DEI for nine countries (AT, CZ, DE, FR, HR, LT, PT, RO, SI). Its ratio to the benchmark is lower than that of the total footprint, and the DEI higher: for France, 0.77 with the variant, against 0.72 in the reference. The variant approaches the WP’s NRRI object without a benchmark of the same scope.
L'analyse publie aussi les scores des co: The analysis also publishes the scores of the EFI and NRRI components for each country that has their series: the EFI according to the normalization and the aggregation between its sub-indicators, the NRRI according to the normalization and the benchmark. The EFI is thus computed for 20 countries and the NRRI for 27. In the reference configuration, the EFI ranges from 0.76 (Netherlands) to 0.26 (Ireland), the NRRI from 0.96 (Netherlands) to 0.32 (Finland).
Configuration de référence, IBD supposé: Reference configuration, BDI assumed equal to 1. The DEI is the geometric mean of the BDI, the EFI and the NRRI; a test in the repository checks that the three columns satisfy this relation.
Dans 15 des 20 pays complets, l'IEE est: In 15 of the 20 complete countries, the EFI is lower than the NRRI; the exceptions are Austria, Finland, Portugal, Romania and Sweden. With the benchmarks retained, the component for pressures on ecosystems is the one that most often pulls the DEI down.
<b>Niveau 1.</b> Avec un IBD supposé au: Level 1. With a BDI assumed to be at most 1, the DEI does not exceed 0.92 in the grid; it reaches 1.31 with an assumed BDI of 2. The CO2 footprint exceeds its benchmark by a factor of 2.5 to 7.0. Crossing level 1 therefore depends on the assumed value of the BDI.
<b>Annulation.</b> 224 configurations su: Cancellation. 224 of the 480 configurations give a zero DEI for all countries: 160 with linear normalization, which removes all discriminating power in the sample, and 64 with a BDI assumed to be zero. For ρ ≤ 0, a zero is transmitted to the DEI, in accordance with §6.2.
<b>Compensation interne.</b> Avec une mo: Internal compensation. With a mean, a sub-indicator below its benchmark partly offsets the overshoot of the others. This is a property of aggregation; the choice of the aggregation function arises at both stages (T3), and the single-stage experiment shows that each one shifts the ranking.
<b>Ce qui déplace le classement.</b> La: What shifts the ranking. Ratio normalization gives a rank correlation of 0.997 (inverted pairs: PT/DE, HU/SE); aggregations with lower substitutability and the weightings change the ranking more (lowest correlation: 0.653).
<b>Poids de l'inconnue IBD.</b> Un IBD c: Weight of the unknown BDI. A common BDI changes the levels without changing the ranking, by construction. A country-specific BDI shifts it: at 0.5 for IT, the others at 1, that country moves from rank 2 to rank 14. As long as the BDI is not measured, DEI levels and rankings are conditional on this assumption.
Le module analyse/evolution_ied.py prolo: The analyse/evolution_ied.py module extends the analysis over time, with the same sub-indicators, benchmarks and functions. Each year is measured with its own data only, without carrying over a neighbouring year, and the benchmarks remain fixed; the populations are those of each year. The countries complete every year from 2015 to 2023 form a panel of 16 countries. For the equally weighted geometric mean and a constant BDI, the change in the logarithm of the DEI splits exactly between the EFI and the NRRI (one third of the change in the logarithm of each); the direction of change is also computed for the 96 configurations of the grid in which the BDI equals 1.
Configuration de référence, IBD supposé: Reference configuration, BDI assumed equal to 1 and constant. EFI and NRRI shares: contributions to the change in the logarithm of the DEI. The remaining configurations, in which the DEI does not change, are mainly those of linear normalization, which cancels it in both years. Detail by year and by sub-indicator: calibration/EVOLUTION_IED.md.
<b>Sens.</b> En configuration de référen: Direction. In the reference configuration, the DEI rises for 12 of the 16 countries in the panel; for 9 of them, no configuration gives a decline. It falls in all configurations for two countries (HR, RO).
<b>Composantes.</b> Dans 10 des 12 pays: Components. In 10 of the 12 rising countries, the contribution of the EFI exceeds that of the NRRI: the decline in mineral nitrogen and phosphorus inputs and in the CO2 footprint accounts for most of the change, the total material footprint varying little.
<b>Lecture.</b> Une hausse de l'IED trad: Reading. A rise in the DEI reflects a fall in measured pressures per inhabitant, relative to fixed benchmarks; levels remain below 1 and the biophysical state is not measured. These series bound past trends; they inform neither the response of S to the regulation coefficient nor the dynamics F. Breaks in series or different definitions affect terms for three countries over the period (AT, PL, SK).
7. Échelle géographique, zones tampons e: 7. Geographical scale, buffer zones and accuracy of representation
Les résultats sont calculés par État mem: The results are computed by Member State because that is the scale at which statistics are published. Biophysical processes have their own scales: a State coincides neither with a river basin, nor with a habitat, nor with a supply chain. In HE’s design, the DEI is attached to a geographical zone linked to the others by buffer zones: a large part of living systems knows no borders and falls within several zones of influence. Fish populations, for example, extend along the coasts of several countries and offshore.
Deux principes distincts relient un terr: Two distinct principles link a territory to the rest of the world. The footprint (materials, CO<sub>2</sub>) attributes to a country’s final demand pressures exerted elsewhere: this is a responsibility rule. The continuity of environments — river basins, seas, species ranges — links territories through their biophysical interactions: this is the object of buffer zones. No national series represents this continuity. Buffer zones require a geometry, spatial data and a rule for sharing the state of a buffer zone between the zones it links; they are to be defined during the construction of HE’s indicators. The existing cross-border divisions shown on the map (section 8) provide real geometries on which to reason; the resolution of observations depends, for its part, on the data integrated.
Les résultats de la calibration sont por: The calibration results are shown on the repository’s map, published by GitHub Pages (benexn.github.io/Europe-Civilization). An “EH” button opens a panel; each view has a direct link, of the form #eh=ied.20002, which identifies the index displayed and the configuration selected. The panel recalls at the top that no value on the map is a measurement of the DEI.
<b>Indices par scénario.</b> La carte co: Indices by scenario. The map colours each country by the DEI, EFI or NRRI of one configuration of the grid, chosen by normalization, aggregation, weightings, NRRI benchmark and assumed BDI: all 480 configurations are accessible. Choices with no effect on the displayed index are disabled. For the DEI, a table gives for each country the scenario value, the reference, the scenario envelope and the Eurostat flags of the terms used.
<b>Rapports aux repères.</b> Chaque sous: Ratios to benchmarks. Each sub-indicator (CO2 footprint, total material footprint, which measures the NRRI, non-renewable material footprint as a variant, nitrogen, phosphorus) can colour the map by its ratio to a benchmark, for all countries that have the series.
<b>Lentilles.</b> Un groupe « Économie H: Lenses. A “Homeostatic Economics” group in the lens selector gives these indices and ratios in the reference configuration. The BDI appears there, disabled: it is not measured and enters the scenarios only as an assumed value.
<b>Écodotations.</b> Un exercice monétai: Ecodotations. A monetary exercise, which can be activated, is described in section 9.5.
L'échelle de couleur des indices est fix: The colour scale of the indices is fixed on [0, 2], with the value 1 at the centre, so that a country’s position relative to the reference level remains legible from one scenario to another. Ratios to benchmarks use a logarithmic scale centred on 1.

Le WP (§4.2) distribue la création monét: The WP (§4.2) distributes primary money creation, the ecodotation, between three channels indexed on the DEI: ESTA = DEI × βpub × c for the State; a citizens’ endowment whose total, for each State, is equal to its public endowment; EFIR = DEI × 𝒴 for each firm, where 𝒴 is measured by its operating expenses (excluding taxes, insurance, financial income and profit distribution) smoothed over the last three years. The global endowment GE = ETSTA + ETCIT + ETFIR is a gross flow of primary creation; it does not correspond to the money stock in circulation, which also depends on the inherited stock, demurrage and secondary creation. In the formalization (§5.5), βpub, c and 𝒴 define the reference primary flow ebase, modulated by the regulation coefficient: e = u · ebase, with u = Φ(DEI); u = 1 is the neutral regime.
Sur la calibration de ces flux, le WP po: On the calibration of these flows, the WP sets out four elements:
<b>Statut des valeurs.</b> Les valeurs n: Status of the values. The numerical values, including the level of ecodotation, are exploratory orders of magnitude, a starting point for modelling and sensitivity analysis; their empirical determination falls within a research programme based on macroeconomic analysis, institutional conditions and the biophysical constraints specific to each context (§4.2).
<b>β<sub>pub</sub>.</b> La valeur de 22: βpub. The value of €22,000 (constant monetary value, base 2017, note 47) is an initial calibration point open to variation and sensitivity study; the amounts of primary creation and ecodotation are expressed at constant monetary value.
<b>Architecture et calibrage.</b> La tri: Architecture and calibration. The three-way division of the channels belongs to the framework’s architecture; their relative weight — βpub, the parity between ETCIT and ETSTA, the base 𝒴 — belongs to calibration. The definition of the base of 𝒴, of its smoothing method and of its calibration elements is a research question.
<b>Problème E2.</b> La calibration des c: Problem E2. The calibration of the ecodotation coefficients is an empirical problem of the programme: on what empirical bases to calibrate these parameters, and what effects different values produce on primary creation flows, distribution, prices, economic activity and compliance with viability constraints. The aim is to characterize parameter ranges compatible with the macroeconomic and biophysical functioning sought; the relation between money creation, real production and the value of money belongs to the same problem.
Le calcul qui suit applique ces formules: The calculation that follows applies these formulas as the WP writes them. It provides E2 with a first order of magnitude and leaves to calibration the choices that the WP refers to it.
Le canal entreprises ne demande, pour un: The firm channel requires, for a zone, only the total of <font name="Math">𝒴</font>: ETFIR = DEI × Σ<font name="Math">𝒴</font>. The eh_entreprises module approximates it using the national accounts by institutional sector (nasa_10_nf_tr, millions of current euros), which cover the 27 countries on the same basis as GDP: intermediate consumption (P2), compensation of employees (D1) and consumption of fixed capital (P51C), of non-financial (S11) and financial (S12) corporations. These gross operating expenses exclude financial charges, taxes and profit distributions; financial corporations enter with their operating expenses only. Two variants are computed: without consumption of fixed capital; non-financial corporations only. Reading requires the expected unit, frequency and direction of each transaction and stops with an error if the table’s schema changes.
C'est un proxy de la somme des <font nam: It is a proxy for the sum of the WP’s <font name="Math">𝒴</font>. It does not include the unincorporated enterprises of the household sector (S14); intermediate consumption includes insurance and financial intermediation services; consumption of fixed capital in the national accounts is an economic measure, distinct from accounting depreciation. These gaps work in opposite directions: their net effect cannot be determined without a bridge table between company accounts, national accounts and eligible items (section 12.2).
β<sub>pub</sub> de référence (22 589 € c: The reference βpub (€22,589 constant 2017, section 4) is converted into current 2023 euros by the same deflator, i.e. €27,242, to be related to current GDP (nama_10_gdp). 𝒴 is smoothed over 2021–2023 according to the same constant-monetary-value convention as βpub: each vintage is expressed at 2023 value by the EU-27 GDP deflator, then the average of the three vintages is formed. The analyse/ecodotations.py module computes each channel and GE relative to 2023 GDP, at the reference flow (u = 1) and at u = Φ0(DEI) of the reference configuration.
<b>Comptage par producteur.</b> Les cons: Counting by producer. Intermediate consumption is counted at each producer: a good enters the expenses of each firm that buys it along the production chain. Σ𝒴 therefore exceeds the value added of an economy. Outsourcing or splitting an activity, a circumvention strategy examined in §7.4 of the WP, adds a stage to this chain and increases the base for unchanged final production.
Année 2023, en part du PIB. Assiette <fo: Year 2023, as a share of GDP. Reference base 𝒴, smoothed at constant value. u = Φ0(national DEI), reference configuration of section 6 (BDI assumed equal to 1). The aggregates relate the sum of the amounts to the sum of GDPs. Bulgaria: 2023 sector accounts not yet published. Batch calibration-eh-20261128T0719Z.
<b>Ordre de grandeur de Σ<font name=\"Ma: Order of magnitude of Σ𝒴. At the reference flow, ETFIR ranges from 85% of GDP (Greece) to 171% (Malta), and reaches 306% in Luxembourg, where the operating expenses of financial corporations, a sector that includes investment funds and group holding companies, represent 151% of GDP. Across 26 countries, it is 133% of GDP. Without consumption of fixed capital, it falls by about ten points (France: 124%). Smoothing at constant value raises the base in this period of rising prices: for France, 135% of GDP against 127% with the average of current amounts.
<b>Dotation globale.</b> Au flux de réfé: Global endowment. At the reference flow, GE ranges from 189% of GDP (Ireland) to 434% (Romania), 273.8% across 26 countries (266.4% with the average of current amounts); at u = national DEI, it is 201% of the GDP of the nineteen complete countries whose accounts are published. The annual flow of primary creation would thus exceed GDP; GE is a flow of money creation and GDP a flow of value added, and their ratio measures neither disposable income nor expenditure.
<b>Lien avec la fonte.</b> À flux consta: Link with demurrage. At constant flows, the monetary component tends towards M* = (e + R)/λ (§5.5): the order of magnitude of GE sets that of M* for a given demurrage, which links E2 to E1. In this relation, λ is, as in §5.5, the rate of demurrage on holdings alone. Demurrage on transactions, a constituent of the architecture and deferred in the V1.0 formalization, dissipates in proportion to the flow of transactions: an M*/GDP ratio computed with λ alone describes the reduced model, not HE’s money stock.
<b>Canal État et harmonisation.</b> DTET: State channel and harmonization. ETSTA/GDP = βpub / GDP per inhabitant: the State channel exceeds GDP as soon as GDP per inhabitant is below βpub (€27,242 current in 2023) — 185% in Bulgaria, 162% in Romania, against 22% in Luxembourg. The same amount per citizen, applied to economies with different levels of output and prices, brings out the question of the system’s harmonization. With the PPS variant (section 4.2), the same purchasing power per citizen is converted back for each country by its 2023 price level index: the State channel falls to 93% of GDP in Bulgaria, 77% in Romania, 77% in Poland, 60% in France and 24% in Luxembourg; GE at the reference flow ranges from 188% (Ireland) to 354% (Luxembourg). The gap between countries narrows; it remains, driven by GDP per inhabitant in volume and by the corporate base.
Dans l'exercice, l'IED qui sert aux dota: In the exercise, the DEI used for the endowments can be that of each country or that of the economic zone. The zone here consists of the twenty countries that have all the series (AT, BG, CZ, DE, ES, FI, FR, HR, HU, IE, IT, LT, LV, NL, PL, PT, RO, SE, SI, SK): it is an availability subset, not the EU-27, for which Eurostat does not publish sector accounts. The zone’s physical quantities per inhabitant are aggregated first — average of national values weighted by 2023 population — then normalized and aggregated like those of a country, for the 480 configurations. It is a proxy: a national value carried over from an earlier year is weighted by the 2023 population.
En configuration de référence, l'IED de: In the reference configuration, the zone DEI is 0.70 (CO2 footprint of 6.8 t/inh, fixed nitrogen 22.3 kg/inh, mineral phosphorus 1.9 kg/inh, total material footprint 14.2 t/inh). With a common u, the endowment depends, from one country to another, only on βpub, population and 𝒴: compared with the national scale, GE goes from 240% to 305% of GDP for Romania and from 264% to 240% for Portugal; across the nineteen countries of the zone whose accounts are published, it is 193% of GDP. The choice of scale shifts the distribution between the countries of the zone, and the effect of a local improvement on u then depends on its share in the total; this joins the attribution principle of the EFI and the definition of buffer zones (section 7).

Un lot n'est enregistré que si les table: A batch is recorded only if the required tables are present and up to date, if the post-computation checks pass, if the integrity of its archive is verified — fingerprint of each raw response against its manifest, and of the archive against the batch reference — and if its offline replay yields the same series and the same results (sensitivity analysis, ecodotations, change over time). The archive is published, then downloaded and verified, before the results are recorded; otherwise the last published batch stays in place.
